title: Smoking effects table
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 109 (Smoking effects table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 109: Smoking and the gas exchange system. To understand the biological effects of smoking on the lungs and circulatory system

head: Substance
Effect
rows: addiction; narrows blood vessels; raises heart rate and blood pressure

questions.q: Explain why smokers become breathless. [3 marks]
questions.a: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin, reducing oxygen carried (1); emphysema reduces alveolar surface area (1); so less oxygen reaches respiring cells (1).
questions.model: Point 1: CO takes the place of oxygen on haemoglobin. Point 2: damaged alveoli give less surface for diffusion. Link: less oxygen reaches the muscles, so the person is breathless.

questions.q: From the chart, how many times more likely is lung cancer in someone smoking 25+ a day?
Which substance in smoke is addictive?
Core: Make a table: substance in smoke, part of the body affected, effect, disease.
questions.a: Tar: airways, cilia, mucus, bronchitis and cancer; nicotine: heart and vessels, CHD; CO: blood, less oxygen.
questions.model: Teacher fills tar first: airways and alveoli; damages cilia and causes mutations; bronchitis and lung cancer.

questions.q: Extend: Explain how smoking increases the risk of coronary heart disease. [4 marks] Use the portal response box.
questions.a: Chemicals damage the artery lining (1); fatty deposits build up, narrowing coronary arteries (1); less blood and oxygen reach heart muscle (1); risk of heart attack (1). CO and nicotine also raise heart rate and blood pressure.

questions.q: Stretch: The chart shows correlation. What other evidence shows smoking causes lung cancer?
questions.a: Tar contains carcinogens shown to cause mutations; risk falls after stopping; dose-response pattern.

questions.q: Big question: why does smoking damage both the lungs and the heart?
questions.a: Tar and particles damage airways and alveoli; nicotine and CO damage arteries and reduce oxygen supply to the heart.
